subject: Urgent: Hightower reserved throughput blocked by GPU pool saturation
messages:
From: Victor Chen <ops@hightower.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hightower Systems Support <support@hightower.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Major latency + errors on dedicated pool - production impact

Chloe / Redwood team,

We have a severe production impact right now. Since ~08:45 PT our inference pipelines have seen unbounded latency spikes (p95 > 2.5s -> p95 > 7s) and a sharp increase in 5xx errors. Our dashboard shows the reserved capacity token consumption dropping even though our traffic is stable — requests are queueing and timing out. This is on our dedicated GPU pool (reference: HW-DP-01).

Attached are latency graphs and example traces (hightower_latency_graphs_0915.png). Support ticket INF-6382 has some logs but we need an immediate remediation path. This is blocking customer-facing flows (recommendations, serving). We are scrambling internally and procurement is already drafting escalation language.

Please confirm receipt and a short ETA for mitigation (we need something within the hour).

-Victor
Head of Platform Engineering
Hightower Systems

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Major latency + errors on dedicated pool - production impact

Team — forwarding Victor's note below. This is high priority, customer on Dedicated/reserved capacity (deal HW-2026-09). Key asks: 1) immediate triage and mitigation to restore Hightower throughput, 2) short-term capacity relief or fallback to keep their production routes alive, and 3) written statement to procurement about what we can commit (credits / SLA exceptions).

Quoted from Victor: "Please confirm receipt and a short ETA for mitigation (we need something within the hour)."

Immediate suggestions:
- Identify if any runaway jobs are holding GPUs (long contexts, very large batch).
- Temporarily preempt lower-priority pools and route Hightower traffic to warm nodes in other pools.
- If necessary, enable model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model for their production route.

Marissa / Aditya / David — confirm who's taking point and post ETA by 09:40. I'll loop procurement if we need formal credit language.

-Chloe
Director, Customer Success (Sales Escalations)
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Major latency + errors on dedicated pool - production impact

Chloe / team — quick diagnostic and actions we've applied: 
- Observed sustained KV-cache growth on cluster gpu-eu-03 (warm nodes) from a long-context batch job that began at 08:30; that job pinned >80% of VRAM on two cards and prevented normal request batching.
- Identified 12 long-running inference sessions from a single Hightower job (likely a misconfiguration client-side with streaming sessions not closing).

Immediate remediation completed (09:45):
- Killed the runaway sessions and cleared KV cache on affected nodes.
- Migrated Hightower production routes off gpu-eu-03 to warm nodes in gpu-us-12 (cold-to-warm spin took ~6 minutes).
- Enabled model-variant fallback for non-critical routes (reduced per-token cost but maintains functional responses).
- Applied short-term preemption policy to reclaim 2x GPU slots from lower-priority tenants (informing billing later).

Impact: latency p95 improved from ~7s to ~1.2s within 12 minutes after mitigation; 5xx rate dropped to baseline. We're continuing to monitor. Runbook snapshot attached (runbook_pool_snapshot_0916.txt).

Remaining asks:
- Aditya: can ops confirm whether the dedicated pool has headroom to support a sustained 20% uplift for Hightower for the next 72 hours?
- David: please prepare a concise note we can send to procurement with timeline and credit options if SLA breach is possible.

Will update in 30 minutes.

-Marissa
Sr. Incident Response Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <procurement@hightower.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Major latency + errors on dedicated pool - production impact

Chloe — following up from procurement. We appreciate the quick remediation on the engineering side, but this outage materially impacted several customer SLA commitments. Procurement needs written confirmation of the following before we proceed with any temporary capacity changes: 
1) Will Redwood commit to honoring the reserved throughput in our contract (HW-2026-09) for the remainder of the quarter?
2) If you cannot guarantee throughput, what credit or make-good are you prepared to offer?
3) Timeline and assurance for capacity expansion or permanent remediation so this doesn't recur.

We need this in writing within 24 hours to avoid pausing our contract renewal conversations. Forwarding our internal legal note for clarity.

- Elena Morales
Procurement Lead
Hightower Systems

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec escalation: Hightower reserved-throughput assurance + path to remediation (need leadership signoff)

Team — we need rapid executive attention and a firm response to procurement. Timeline below (summary of what happened + recommended commitments):

Summary:
- 09/15 08:30 PT: runaway long-context job pinned VRAM on warm nodes in the dedicated pool serving Hightower, causing queueing and errors.
- 09/15 09:45 PT: remediation actions restored baseline performance (Marissa).
- 09/16 11:20 PT: Procurement requested written assurances and possible credits.

Customer asks: 
- Written confirmation that reserved throughput will be honored for the quarter.
- A transparent credit/make-good proposal for the impacted window.
- Timeline for a capacity remediation plan (permanent fix).

Recommended actions for leadership signoff: 
1) Commit to honoring reserved throughput for Hightower through Q4 while we execute a capacity-scaling plan. This will likely require an immediate temporary capacity reserve: reserve +20% headroom on gpu-us-12 (estimated incremental cost $7.5k/week) while we provision additional nodes.
2) Offer a one-time credit equal to 10% of the monthly committed fee for September to address the outage window (we can adjust after legal input).
3) Ops to deliver a 30-day remediation plan: hardware spin-up timeline, improved preemption rules to prevent VRAM pinning from single-tenant jobs, and a customer-facing runbook describing fallback behavior.

Attachments: SOW_redline_v2.pdf (procurement request), runbook_pool_snapshot_0916.txt, INF-6382 link.

Please confirm approval or propose edits. If approved, I'll draft the procurement response and loop Legal/Finance for the credit.

-Chloe
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
